chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr narrated from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A well is drawn from, wudu (ablution) was performed with it, clothes were washed from it, and dough was kneaded with it, then it became known that there had been a dead body in it. He said: “There is no harm, the garment is not to be washed, and the salat (prayer) performed with it is not to be repeated.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: If a human being dies in a well or in a pond whose water is less than the amount of a kurr, and the water does not change because of that, then seventy buckets should be drawn from it, and it becomes purified after that. His mentioning the pond together with the well means thereby a pond that has a supply through springing from the earth; whatever is of this kind takes the ruling of wells. As for when it has no supply, then its use is not permissible if something that renders it impure falls into it whenever it is less than a kurr. What he mentioned is indicated by this.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the ritual prayer performed using that water
key_terms.الْكُرِّ: the legal measure of water used to determine impurity rulings
key_terms.بِئْرٌ: a well from which water is drawn
key_terms.سَبْعُونَ دَلْوًا: the prescribed number of buckets to be drawn for purification
key_terms.غَدِيرٍ: a pond, here specifically one discussed in relation to well rulings
key_terms.مَادَّةٌ: a continuing source or supply of water from the earth
key_terms.مَيِّتٌ: a dead body found in the water

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using well water if a dead body is later discovered in it?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal ruling of water drawn from a well later discovered to have contained a dead body, stating that prior acts done with it do not need to be redone. The accompanying juristic note clarifies the purification ruling for wells and spring-fed ponds, especially when the water is less than a kurr and affected by impurity.
